title: Apple GPU RMSNorm baseline characterization
question: How does the existing Apple GPU RMSNorm implementation scale across decode, batched-decode-like, and prefill row counts, and what limits representative regimes?

correctness.command: MODULAR_DEBUG=device-sync-mode uv run --locked mojo run -I src -I tests tests/test_rms_norm.mojo
correctness.acceptance_formula: finite(actual) and finite(expected) and abs(actual - expected) <= atol + rtol * abs(expected)
correctness.benchmark_guard: All-ones input and weight must produce finite BF16 ones for every timed workload before measurement.

workload_contract.buffer_reuse: One input, weight, and output allocation is reused for all warmup and retained iterations of a workload.
workload_contract.observed_hardware_traffic: Not inferred from either source-level formula; report only named profiler counters.

workloads.semantic_role: hypothetical batched decode; not current V0 behavior
hypothetical batched decode; not current V0 behavior

measurement_protocol.decisive_command: uv run --locked python benchmarks/run_rms_norm.py --blocks 4 --experiment-id EXP-0001 --run-id EXP-0001-RUN-001 --recorded --output-dir <absolute-external-path>/EXP-0001-RUN-001
measurement_protocol.timing_boundary: One enqueue_rms_norm_apple_gpu dispatch measured through max.benchmark.bencher_iter_custom, including GPU completion required by that GPU-aware bencher.
excluded: Mojo compilation and pipeline creation before the benchmark

environment.reason: Headline timing uses the GPU-aware bencher rather than globally forcing every device operation to synchronize.

measurement_protocol.sample_definition: One reported max.benchmark repetition value in milliseconds per dispatch; retain its actual internal iteration count.
measurement_protocol.throughput_rule: Recompute throughput from the retained latency sample and the exact row-by-hidden work definition; do not treat logical bytes as observed DRAM traffic.

calibration.policy: Run one exploratory ascending/descending pair before decisive collection. Calibration output is not retained as experiment evidence.
calibration.pass_condition: All workloads parse to the declared schema, actual iteration counts are retained, and the final five repetitions show no persistent monotonic warmup trend large enough to obscure row-count scaling.
calibration.failure_action: Stop before decisive collection, amend the protocol in a new commit, and explain the deviation.

observed.result: The parser and order checks passed. Small-row half-block shifts changed direction between blocks rather than showing persistent warmup drift; rows 2048 and 4096 were stable within each block.
observed.evidence_boundary: Exploratory dirty-worktree, battery-powered output was intentionally not retained and supports no performance claim.

environment_requirements.runtime_device: DeviceContext.name() must identify the Apple GPU
environment_requirements.thermal: no recorded thermal or performance warning
environment_requirements.system_load: reasonably idle; no deliberate competing CPU or GPU workload
environment_requirements.display_policy: record attached displays and keep the configuration unchanged across all four blocks

profiling_protocol.tool: Xcode Metal System Trace through xctrace
profiling_protocol.timing_use: diagnostic only; instrumented durations are not headline benchmark results
workload_selection: the measured transition workload between underfill and scaling
profiling_protocol.generated_code: Retain compact compiler-output provenance and checksums when available; keep large dumps outside Git.
profiling_protocol.counter_rule: Name every counter and its capture procedure. If a required signal is unavailable, record the mechanism as unresolved instead of substituting a source-level estimate.

profiling_calibration.summary: Rows=1 generated-code and Metal trace paths were validated. The emitted kernel preserves the 512-byte shared tree and nine workgroup barriers. The stock trace had no counter set, and the direct Metal GPU Counters instrument selected a profile unsupported on this target, so hardware traffic and stall mechanisms remain unresolved.
profiling_calibration.evidence_boundary: Battery-powered tooling calibration only; no headline timing or optimization decision.

baseline_measurement.summary: The dispatch floor extends through r128-h896. r512-h896 is the first workload above that floor in every same-order block. Logical work throughput still increased from r2048-h896 to r4096-h896, so saturation was not observed within the frozen range.

completion_conditions: The full RMSNorm oracle test passes at the measurement commit.
All four blocks prove the Apple GPU and Metal runtime identity.
Each workload has 40 valid raw samples with block, repetition, value, unit, and internal iteration count.
The environment requirements hold without an unrecorded deviation.
Representative Metal traces or an explicit tooling limitation are recorded with provenance.
The report bounds supported scaling observations and separates causal findings from unresolved mechanisms.
stop_conditions: The runtime device or API identity is not Apple GPU plus Metal.
The repository is dirty for a decisive block.
AC power or thermal requirements fail.
The benchmark output cannot be parsed without losing a repetition or its iteration count.
Calibration shows unresolved warmup drift or noise that obscures the row-count comparison.
nonclaims: No decoder-block, model-phase, end-to-end inference, time-to-first-token, or time-per-output-token result.
No claim that logical or program-requested bytes equal observed cache, fabric, or DRAM traffic.
No causal bottleneck claim from timing alone.
No claim that batched-decode-like workloads are implemented by V0.

artifacts.evidence_use: Method validation and structural generated-code observation only.
AC-powered operation-level scaling, noise, transition-workload selection, and saturation non-observation.
